title: Coherent uniqueness of contravariant transport along an edge
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors and natural equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cartesian fibrations as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to B$ be a cartesian fibration of quasicategories, let $f:b\to b'$ be an edge of $B$, and put $E_b=E\times_B\{b\}$ and $E_{b'}=E\times_B\{b'\}$. Suppose $R_0,R_1:E_{b'}\to E_b$ have coherent witnesses $h_j:\Delta^1\times E_{b'}\to E$ satisfying $p h_j=f\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^1}$, with endpoints $i_b\circ R_j$ at $0$ and $i_{b'}$ at $1$, where $i_b:E_b\hookrightarrow E$ and $i_{b'}:E_{b'}\hookrightarrow E$ are the fiber inclusions, and with $p$-cartesian edges at every vertex. Then $R_0$ and $R_1$ are equivalent objects in $\operatorname{Fun}(E_{b'},E_b)$. In particular, there are coherent transformations $s:R_0\to R_1$ and $t:R_1\to R_0$ with inverse homotopies $ts\simeq1_{R_0}$ and $st\simeq1_{R_1}$ in this functor quasicategory. No cocartesian structure or adjunction is assumed.
